slides.subtitle:
September CPI lands today.
Fed funds rate now 3.75% to 4.00%.

slides.title: What Just Happened?
slides.big: The Fed raised rates by 0.25 points to 3.75% to 4.00%.
slides.body: Sep 16, 2026. A unanimous 12-0 vote and the first hike since July 2023. Most officials expect another by year-end.

slides.title: Let's Look at the Numbers
slides.subtitle: US CPI inflation (% year over year)
slides.body: Gasoline drove over a third of August's monthly gain.
slides.source: Source: BLS (Jul, Aug). *Sep = economist consensus, per CNBC.

slides.title: Why Should You Care?
slides.body: Higher gas prices push CPI up, which puts more pressure on the Fed to hike again. Higher rates also make loans and mortgages more expensive.

slides.title: The Bottom Line
items: Inflation now steers the Fed's next move.
Gas prices are the short-term swing factor.
